abstract: Understanding the genetic factors influencing estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is crucial for developing effective prevention and treatment strategies. This study aimed to identify genetically prioritized candidate factors influencing eGFR leveraging large-scale genomic datasets. Genome-wide association study (GWAS) data from the eQTLGen Consortium (30,000+ individuals) and the CKDGen/UK Biobank (over 1.2 million individuals) were analyzed. A total of 16,987 cis-expression quantitative trait loci (cis-eQTL) genes, obtained from the eQTLGen Consortium, were utilized as the exposure traits in this study. The creatinine-based eGFR served as the outcome phenotype in this study. The enrichment analysis, two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), and reverse MR were conducted to explore functional pathways. We identified 1,818 genes causally associated with eGFR, including 953 positively and 865 negatively correlated genes. The enrichment analysis underscored the role of adherens junction pathways and glucose metabolic processes in regulating eGFR. Further, two-sample MR and reverse MR validated 210 significant genes associated with eGFR. This study provided new insights into the genetic basis of eGFR, identifying a series of potential biomarkers. The findings suggested the roles of adherens junctions and glucose metabolism in kidney function. Further research is needed to validate these findings and explore their clinical implications.
